title: Remote-work etiquette
examples: What is the best way to handle urgent questions when I am in a different time zone?
How can I make sure my team knows when I am actually available to respond?
Should I always use email for non-urgent updates, or is instant messaging better?

explain.say: Today we are learning about asynchronous communication in remote work.

items: Communication does not need to happen instantly.
It allows people to work at different times.

explain.say: Think about sending a detailed project update via email.
This method lets the receiver read and respond when it is convenient for them.
A recorded video walkthrough of a process is another great example.
In real life, scheduling a meeting for a global team is an async challenge.
A common mistake is expecting an immediate reply to a detailed message.

faq.q: If I send an email, how long should I wait for a reply?
faq.a: Generally, allow a full business day for a detailed email response. You might also ask, 'What is a reasonable response time for an email?' or 'How long should I wait for written feedback?'
asks: How fast should I expect a reply?
What is the expected turnaround time?

faq.q: Does asynchronous communication mean I should never use instant messaging?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but you should reserve instant messaging for truly urgent matters only. You could also ask, 'When is it okay to use chat?' or 'What is the difference between urgent and non-urgent?'
asks: When should I use chat vs email?

faq.q: How do I signal that a message requires deep thought, not just a quick answer?
faq.a: Use clear subject lines or opening statements to set expectations about the required effort. You might also ask, 'How do I signal complexity?' or 'What phrasing shows deep thought is needed?'
asks: How to ask for detailed input?
How to make it clear this is not a quick question?

faq.q: What if the time difference is extreme, like between Australia and New Zealand?
faq.a: Always reference time zones clearly when setting deadlines or suggesting meeting times. You could ask, 'How do I handle large time gaps?' or 'What time zone format should I use?'
asks: How to write dates across time zones?

faq.q: Should I summarize key decisions in a follow-up email after a discussion?
faq.a: Yes, summarizing action items keeps everything documented and asynchronous. You could also ask, 'Should I write up meeting notes?' or 'What should the follow-up email contain?'
asks: What is the purpose of a summary email?

facts: Asynchronous communication does not require all parties to be online simultaneously.
Email is best suited for non-urgent, detailed information sharing.
Recording process walkthroughs are excellent forms of async knowledge transfer.
Setting clear expectations about response times is key to remote etiquette.

quiz.say: You need to send a comprehensive report that requires careful reading and thoughtful feedback. Which method is most appropriate?
quiz.why: Email allows the recipient time to read the detailed report thoroughly before composing a thoughtful reply.

wrong.0: Instant messaging implies an expectation of immediate attention, which is not suitable for detailed reports.
wrong.1: A live call requires everyone to be available at the exact same time, defeating the purpose of asynchronous work.
wrong.2: Voicemails are often difficult to reference later or to attach supporting documents to.

quiz.say: A team member in India needs to review a document that you created in the US. To respect time zones, what should you do?

options.show: Send it late in the day your time
options.say: Send it late in the day your time

options.show: Write the deadline in both time zones
options.say: Write the deadline in both time zones

options.show: Ask them to check their local time
options.say: Ask them to check their local time

quiz.why: Stating the deadline in both local time zones removes ambiguity for the recipient.

wrong.0: This might mean it arrives too late for them to start working on it that day.
wrong.2: This assumes the recipient knows your local time zone, which is not always true.
wrong.3: This puts the burden of time zone calculation entirely on the recipient.

quiz.say: You are documenting a complex software setup process. Which format best supports step-by-step, non-real-time instruction?
quiz.why: A recorded video allows the viewer to pause, rewind, and rewatch complex steps at their own pace.

wrong.1: A long email can be overwhelming and hard to follow sequentially.
wrong.2: Chat messages are too brief and lack the visual context needed for complex processes.
wrong.3: An invitation implies a scheduled, synchronous event rather than self-paced learning.
